newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER - REAL MAKE STUNNING COMEBACK, BARCELONA CRUMBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - REAL MAKE STUNNING COMEBACK, BARCELONA CRUMBLE.

text.p: Real Madrid took a decisive step in pursuit of their 27th Spanish league crown on Wednesday when they overturned a 2-0 deficit to beat bottom-placed Sevilla 4-2.
The win came as second-placed Barcelona crashed 3-1 at Valladolid, leaving Fabio Capello's Real 10 points clear at the top with eight games remaining.
It was the first time in nearly 15 years that Real had come back from two goals down.
On the last occasion legendary Real striker Emilio Butragueno had scored twice to celebrate his first division debut.
"I feel that I have taken part in making history," said Capello afterwards.
The match had looked likely to dent Real's title prospects as Sevilla found gaps overhead and down the flanks to score through teenager Jose Mari and Oulida in the opening 20 minutes.

Capello substituted out-of-form striker Davor Suker for newly-signed utility man Ze Roberto, and was quickly rewarded with a goal when Clarence Seedorf pounced on a back heel from Raul Gonzalez to give keeper Juan Carlos Unzue no chance.
The southerners appealed for offside against Raul in the goal, and were deprived of a clear breakaway opportunity for Jose Mari moments later when the referee blew the halftime whistle.

The southerners seemed to start the second half still suffering from the decisions, and saw Raul knock in the equaliser on the hour, before Fernando Hierro and Predrag Mijatovic finished off the job in the closing minutes.
It was the 11th time this season that Real had came from behind to claim three points.
With Real suffering, the evening had seemed to be going Barcelona's way after Brazilian striker Ronaldo had put his side ahead in the fourth minute.
But coach Bobby Robson's men crumbled under continuous pressure and were sunk by two goals from diminutive Valladolid forward Victor Fernandez.
"They played much better than we did...they could have scored more goals...," said Robson, who said he had been kept informed of the Real Madrid score.
The evening could have been even worse for Barcelona, who had stood to lose second place and with it Spain's second European Cup place for next season, if Real Betis had beaten struggling Zaragoza.
But Betis threw away a two-goal lead for the second successive home game, and had to settle for a 2-2 draw that leaves them one point adrift of the Catalan side.
Sporting Gijon fired coach Benito Floro after going down 4-0 at Athletic Bilbao.
Last-but-one Logrones lost by the same score at Celta Vigo, and seem set to accompany Sevilla down to the second division.
